items.readable_text:
Content:
In this lesson, we'll extend our understanding of angles to real-world and mathematical problems.

Content:
For example, let's find the angle formed by the minute and hour hands of a clock at [MATH: 5]:[MATH: 00,] as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fe07e8e3ab7529a0885f9a1431142ad4]

Content:
If we connect the center of the clock face and the hour marks, we get [MATH: 12] identical angles. And, since a full angle has a measure of [MATH: 360^\circ,] each of these angles has a measure of [MATH: \dfrac{360^\circ}{12}.]

Content:
Now, let's compute the value of this fraction:

Content:
[MATH: (360)/(12)|=; 360 ÷ 12|=; 36 × 10 ÷ 12|=; (36 ÷ 12) × 10|=; 3 × 10|=; 30]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: \dfrac{360^\circ}{12} = 30^\circ.]

Content:
The angle formed by the minute and hour hands of a clock at [MATH: 5]:[MATH: 00] contains [MATH: 5] such angles, so its measure is

Content:
[MATH: 5 \times 30^\circ = 150^\circ.]
